title: A revalidation record's front matter — software-analysis capability
description: The front matter of one revalidation record, a file `<date>-<subject>.md` in `revalidations/` under the analysis location (software-analysis DEC-001 points 5 and 6): one check of some artefacts against one version of the system, kept only when there is something to say — a planned revalidation, or one that finds a gap or a regression. A record is an act, not an anchored artefact: it carries no friction block, and its folder is not a place. It cites artefacts by id, withdrawn ones included. The body gives each artefact's outcome with its justification, then the gaps and what resolved each. It may copy executed results from the evidence point as support for an outcome, never in place of one. Applied by `pkit software-analysis validate`; unknown fields are refused.

change.description: The change that carried the revalidation: a tracked work item (`#123`), a pull request, or a range of commits on the default branch (software-analysis DEC-001 point 6).

trigger.description: What triggered it (DEC-001 point 5): `planned` — a change proposed, before code; `drift` — friction on a pull request; `scheduled` — friction the whole-repository check found; `close` — a pull request changing artefacts or their anchors lands; `onboarding`.

reviewed-against.description: A planned record's only, and required there: where the design it reviewed stood, one mapping for each source of the design (DEC-001 point 6). Each source is named by its title, its link where it lies outside this repository, and its version, a pointer to the text reviewed. A record of another trigger leaves it out.

by.description: Who performed it: a person, or an agent.

confirmed-by.description: The person who confirmed an agent's outcomes — and decided stale against regressed where the two were ambiguous (DEC-001 point 5).

outcomes.description: Each artefact covered, by id, and how its revalidation ended (DEC-001 point 5): `holds`; `analysis-stale` — the change was intended, so the artefact was updated; `code-regressed` — the artefact still describes what is wanted, so a defect was reported; `gap-found` — behaviour nothing describes, or a description with no behaviour.

evidence.description: Optional: the executed results the revalidation drew on, each an entry of the `pkit::analysis:revalidation-evidence` point copied whole, in the point's own entry shape (DEC-001 point 7) — a passing result as support for `holds`, a failing one as a regression's proof. A record copies rather than cites by id: the record is history, while the point holds what its fillers report now, so an id alone would point at nothing once a filler stops reporting that commit. Evidence supports an outcome and never replaces one, so each artefact an entry is for has its outcome above; the check also holds each entry's `id` to its own `<artefact>@<commit>#<check>`.

source.description: One source of the design a planned revalidation reviewed. Without a `url`, it lies in this repository: its `version` is a commit's full id, or `this change` when the design lands in the change that adds the record. With a `url`, it lies outside: its `version` is the time its text was read, or a commit's full id in another repository. These definitions are the one home of each form, so whatever checks a source reads them here.

title.description: What the source is, for the reader.

version.description: The pointer to the text reviewed, never a version number: the capability's artefacts and records carry no declared versions.

link.description: An absolute link: a scheme, `://`, a host, and the rest with no white space. It names no tracker, so checking it needs no knowledge of one.

time.description: When a text was read: a UTC timestamp, as a revalidation's `at` is (COR-050 point 3). Quoted in YAML, which would otherwise read it as a time and not as text.

this-change.description: The change the record lands in, for a design that lands with its record. Its commit is the one that added the record, found from the history as a revalidation's is (DEC-001 point 6; COR-050 point 3).
